name: Sgt. Lowry (or Lowery)
summary: A Special Forces sergeant Larry remembers on top of Núi Bà Đen — the man he reported the enemy digging to on his last day there, and the man who came back an hour later and said, in Larry's words, "You son of a bitch you killed 450 civilians down there!" On 2026-09-02 Larry added what he thinks followed from it: "Somebody up there, probably Sgt Lowery, probably reported me KIA. All the officers were gone, so he was the only one on the other radio in Special Forces that I know of." He also placed him off duty: Larry would meet him at a bar called the Papallon on Tu Do street in Saigon, and says "Lowry usually worked at Body Jab 42 Nui Ba Den." The spelling and the identity are both unresolved.
researchNotes: The spellings are transcriptions by Larry's son of the name as Larry says it; neither is Larry's own rendering, and no spelling of this name yet carries the weight that "Geutler" does for Captain Guegler. THE KIA CONNECTION IS LARRY'S INFERENCE, NOT AN ESTABLISHED FACT, and is recorded that way: he says "probably," twice in one sentence, and reasons to it from who else could have been on a radio that day rather than from anything he witnessed. It is valuable because it is the first mechanism the archive has for how a false report could have been generated at all — a man with radio access, in the aftermath of an accusation, with the officers away — and because it makes one person the hinge of both open questions. It should not harden into a claim about a named man without documentary support. NEGATIVE, and a clean one (2026-09-02): asked whether Lowry's name was painted on the rock in VN-0035, Larry said no — and said no to all six other names read to him, adding that those names "were there when I arrived. I didn't know any of them." The standing instruction to check his name against the roster-rock names is therefore closed, answered by Larry, and the rock is not a route to identifying him. What remains: Special Forces rosters and unit records for Núi Bà Đen and Detachment B-32 in 1964-65, and veteran accounts of the site. Larry separately describes him as an alcoholic (data/recollections/giscus-stories-c18259589.json), and describes Gagne as not getting on with him; that is character evidence from one man about another and is held as such. The accusation day is data/timeline/1965-08-450-civilians-accusation.json.
